description: Flattens raw SteamSpy bulk payloads into a tabular DataFrame for coarse_filter.
docstring:
Flatten bulk payloads into a catalog DataFrame.

Args:
    payloads: RawPayload objects with source='steamspy_all', typically from fetch_steamspy_catalog after persistence, or read back via storage.read_raw_payloads for a re-run of the coarse filter alone.

Returns:
    A DataFrame with columns: appid, name, developer, publisher, positive, negative, owners_low, owners_high, price_usd, initialprice, discount, tags (the raw per-app tag:votes dict, kept for extract_tags in enrichment -- NOT flattened into separate rows here). One row per unique appid; if the same appid appears in more than one input payload (duplicate across pages), the later one in iteration order wins and the occurrence is counted.

Returns also (as a DataFrame attribute or a parallel return, per implementation) a duplicate_appid count for the coarse_filter_contract's rejection_reasons tally -- exact mechanism (DataFrame.attrs vs. a second return value) is an implementation detail left to worker-coder, but the count must be observable by coarse_filter's caller (run_acquisition) for the funnel report.
preconditions: Each RawPayload.payload matches SteamSpy's per-app object shape (missing/absent fields are tolerated and become NaN/None, not a hard failure, since SteamSpy's schema is not strictly documented)
postconditions: appid column has no duplicate values in the output
price_usd and initialprice are floats in dollars (SteamSpy reports price in cents; this function divides by 100), never left as raw cents

edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns an empty DataFrame with the full expected column set

edge_cases.input: The same appid present in two input payloads with different content
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the later one (in iteration order) wins; duplicate_appid tally increments by 1 for each extra occurrence beyond the first

edge_cases.input: A payload missing the 'tags' field entirely
edge_cases.expected_behavior: tags column is an empty dict {} for that row, not NaN or None, so downstream extract_tags can iterate it uniformly

edge_cases.input: price field is the string '0' for a free-to-play title
edge_cases.expected_behavior: price_usd == 0.0, a valid float, not NaN

unit_tests.name: test_flattens_fixture_page_into_expected_columns
unit_tests.description: tests/fixtures/steamspy_all_page0.json parsed into RawPayload objects produces the documented column set with correct dtypes.
unit_tests.expected: DataFrame with exactly the documented columns

unit_tests.name: test_price_cents_converted_to_dollars
unit_tests.description: A raw price of '1999' (cents) becomes price_usd=19.99.

unit_tests.name: test_duplicate_appid_last_wins_and_counted
unit_tests.description: Two payloads for the same appid produce one row (the later content) and a duplicate_appid count of 1.
unit_tests.expected: 1 row matching the later payload; duplicate count == 1

unit_tests.name: test_empty_input_yields_empty_frame_with_columns
unit_tests.description: No payloads at all still returns a DataFrame with the right columns and 0 rows.
